Five-case analytical proofLet  $D$  be an arbitrary dissociation set of  $F_p^-$ , and let  $r$  be the number of selected vertices among  $A_0,A_1,B_0,B_1$ .The proof partitions all possibilities without assuming any symmetry of the witness interface.Case 1:  $r=0$ The induced graph on the relevant vertices is precisely the old  $H_p-e$  model with both unused vertices absent.The preceding all- $p$  cap gives
$$|D|\leq 7p.$$
The four new vertices are absent, so their extra incident edges cannot invalidate the comparison.Case 2:  $r=1$ There are two distinct subcases.A₁ or B₁: virtual  $H_p-e$  comparison.Identify the chosen A₁ (respectively B₁) with the old unused vertex  $u_L$  (respectively  $u_R$ ).Every edge of the comparison graph induced on  $D$  also exists in  $F_p^-$ . The new construction has additional edges, including connections to the opposite-wing centres, which can only impose more dissociation restrictions.Consequently,
$$D\text{ dissociation in }F_p^-
\implies D\text{ dissociation in }H_p-e,$$
and hence  $|D|\leq7p$ .A₀ or B₀: the asymmetric argument.Suppose A₀ is chosen. Since A₀ has at most one selected neighbour in the entire graph, remove that neighbour if it exists.This is a global capacity argument: all left  $x_j,i_j$  are now absent, not merely one such vertex per block.Each left block retains the local configuration
$$a_j,\quad c_j-y_j-b_j,$$
whose contribution is at most  $2+\mathbf 1_{\{a_j\in D\}}$ .Let  $a_L$  count the selected left a-witnesses and  $g_R$  count good right blocks. The other wing contributes at most  $3p+g_R$ . Therefore,
$$|D'|\leq 2p+a_L+3p+g_R.$$
The crucial inequality is
$$\boxed{a_L+g_R\leq p.}$$
Here is the complete predecessor argument.Write  $P_j=(L_j,R_{j+1})$ . If a slot contains both a selected  $a_j^L$  and a good block  $R_{j+1}$ , the complete  $K_{2,2}$  adjacency forces the selected witnesses to be exactly
$$a_j^L,\qquad a_{j+1}^R.$$
They saturate each other. Moreover: $a_j^L$  meets both witnesses of  $R_j$ ; $a_{j+1}^R$  meets both witnesses of  $L_{j-1}$ .Both predecessor blocks must therefore be empty of selected witnesses. Thus the predecessor slot  $P_{j-1}$  contains neither a selected left a-witness nor a good right block.The predecessor map is injective. If  $d_2$  denotes double slots and  $d_0$  empty slots, then
$$d_2\leq d_0,
\qquad
a_L+g_R=p+d_2-d_0\leq p.$$
It follows that
$$|D'|\leq6p.$$
Restoring A₀ and at most one removed neighbour gives
$$|D|\leq6p+2\leq7p.$$

$$\boxed{g_L+a_R\leq p.}$$
A double slot now contains a good left block and a selected right a-witness. The same predecessor relations force the preceding slot empty. $$p+3p=4p.$$

$$|D|\leq4p+2p+2+2
=6p+4\leq7p.$$
The B₀,B₁ case reverses the wings.Case 4: selected added vertices on both sidesChoose one selected A and one selected B. Remove their selected neighbours; their union has size at most two.In each wing, all  $i$ 's and one of  $x,y$  per block are now absent. $$Q=
\bigcup_{j<p}\{c_j,x_j,i_j\}

\bigcup_{j\geq p}\{x_j,y_j,a_j,b_j\}.$$

$$\boxed{\beta_2(F_p^-)=\beta_2(F_p)=7p.}$$
This is an unrestricted dissociation-number result, not merely an optimum within a restricted family of candidate sets.4. The resulting graph is two-connected and spans the witnesses and all  $c,x,y$  vertices.Each A/B vertex can then be adjoined with its  $p$  distinct old  $x$ - or  $y$ -neighbours. b_{0,j+1}^R$$
cyclically. $k=1$ : the link restores the deleted edge  $e$ . The resulting graph is  $F_p$ , already two-connected. $k=2$ : there are two distinct links between the two copies, using distinct ports. Deleting a vertex can destroy at most one of these links; the other still connects the two internally connected pieces. $k\geq3$ : the pieces form a cycle. Deleting one vertex leaves each piece connected and destroys at most one cyclic link, so the remaining links still connect all pieces.Degrees are preserved because each port loses one internal edge and gains one external edge.For the dissociation upper bound, restriction to each copy gives
$$|D|\leq 7p k.$$
Repeating  $Q$  attains this bound: the left port  $b_0^L$  is omitted from  $Q$ , so no new cyclic link has both endpoints selected.Hence the exact unrestricted value is
$$\boxed{\beta_2(G_{p,k})=7pk.}$$
The order, selection size and gap are
$$n=(12p+4)k,\qquad
|S|=8pk,\qquad
d=pk.$$

\left\lfloor
\frac{\Delta n}{12\Delta+10}
\right\rfloor.$$
Substitute
$$\Delta=\frac{5p}{2},
\qquad n=(12p+4)k.$$
Then
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{\Delta n}{12\Delta+10}
&=
\frac{\frac{5p}{2}(12p+4)k}{30p+10}\\
&=
\frac{10p(3p+1)k}{10(3p+1)}\\
&=pk.
\end{aligned}$$
This equals the constructed gap exactly.Since  $p$  is even and  $p\geq6$ ,
$$\Delta=15,20,25,30,\ldots$$
and the claimed sharpness follows along precisely this subfamily.No conclusion about exact SF values or other maximum-degree allowances follows from this argument.7. VerdictI cannot presently establish the all-even- $p$  equality or give a counterexample. The modified construction is a genuinely different extremal problem: the two old  $u$ -vertices have been replaced by four vertices whose selected-neighbour capacities interact across blocks and wings.There is useful positive evidence, but it is not a proof. In particular, I would not accept an argument that simply applies the three local bounds from the attached manuscript independently to the four new vertices.1. What survives immediatelyLet  $G_p^\ast$  denote the modified graph.The original construction gives an explicit dissociation set of size  $7p$ :Left wing: select  $c_j,x_j,i_j$  in every block.Right wing: select  $x_j,y_j,a_j,b_j$  in every block.Select none of  $A_0,A_1,B_0,B_1$ .The selected induced components are isolated vertices and isolated edges. In particular, no cross-witness edge has both endpoints selected.Therefore
$$\boxed{\beta_2(G_p^\ast)\geq 7p.}$$
This lower bound is valid for every even  $p\geq6$ .The original local block edges and witness interface also remain unchanged. The nine-state local table in the attached manuscript, particularly its explicit degree constraints (290)–(297), remains useful. all-p-sharpness.md2. The new global capacity obstructionWrite
$$\alpha_j=[a_j\in D],\qquad
\beta_j=[b_j\in D].$$
For an arbitrary dissociation set  $D$ , define the total selected-neighbour loads
$$\begin{aligned}
\ell(A_0)&=
\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}([i_j^L\in D]+[x_j^L\in D])
+\sum_{j=0}^{p/2-1}[c_j^R\in D],\\
\ell(A_1)&=
\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}([i_j^L\in D]+[y_j^L\in D])
+\sum_{j=p/2}^{p-1}[c_j^R\in D].
\end{aligned}$$
The corresponding right-side expressions are
$$\begin{aligned}
\ell(B_0)&=
\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}([i_j^R\in D]+[x_j^R\in D])
+\sum_{j=0}^{p/2-1}[c_j^L\in D],\\
\ell(B_1)&=
\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}([i_j^R\in D]+[y_j^R\in D])
+\sum_{j=p/2}^{p-1}[c_j^L\in D].
\end{aligned}$$
These are exact, not estimates.The crucial constraints are
$$\boxed{
A_s\in D\implies \ell(A_s)\leq1,
\qquad
B_s\in D\implies \ell(B_s)\leq1.
}$$
In particular,
$$A_0,A_1\in D
\implies
\sum_j[i_j^L\in D]\leq1,$$
and
$$B_0,B_1\in D
\implies
\sum_j[i_j^R\in D]\leq1.$$
These inequalities expose the main difficulty with a naive adaptation of the old proof.The new vertices do not provide one extra selectable neighbour per block. They provide at most one selected neighbour over their entire neighbourhood.3. A useful distinction between the casesLet
$$m=|D\cap\{A_0,A_1,B_0,B_1\}|.$$
There are four fundamentally different situations: $m$ Required treatment0Re-establish the witness-slot argument with no old  $u$ 's1Charge the single connector's capacity globally2–3Account for overlapping and complementary connector neighbourhoods4Use all four global capacity constraints simultaneouslyThe old proof's cases of zero, one and two selected  $u$ 's cannot simply be reused.In particular, the old estimate
$$|D\cap V_T|\leq 2p+2+o_T+f_T$$
was derived using the specific adjacency of one  $u_T$  to all  $p$  isolates and one distinguished  $y$ . It is not a valid estimate for either modified wing without a new derivation.4. Exploratory exact optimizationI also formulated the modified graph as a binary optimization problem.For each vertex  $v$ , introduce  $z_v\in\{0,1\}$ . The dissociation condition is exactly equivalent to
$$\sum_{w\in N(v)}z_w+
(\deg(v)-1)z_v
\leq \deg(v).$$
Maximizing
$$\sum_v z_v$$
therefore gives the unrestricted dissociation number.Exploratory integer optimization returned:Even  $p$ Computed optimum $7p$ 6424285656107070128484Forcing any one of the four new vertices to be selected also produced optima strictly below  $7p$  for  $p=6,8$ .These are exploratory solver results, not independently verified mathematical certificates. They cannot establish the universal assertion.5. The precise missing theoremThe remaining problem is to establish
$$\boxed{
\forall\,p\geq6,\quad
p\text{ even}
\implies
\max_D |D|\leq7p.
}$$
A promising route is to extend the original good/occupied/full-cross-free slot argument with four additional global load variables.The proof needs a simultaneous inequality of the form
$$|D|
\leq
7p-\Phi(D),$$
where  $\Phi(D)\geq0$  accounts for the selected connectors and their globally consumed neighbour capacities.It is not enough to establish four separate local inequalities: the same selected block vertex can contribute to multiple connector loads, and the witness interface creates further exclusions between the wings.The attached manuscript already demonstrates the appropriate methodological principle in its exact interface formula: fix witness states first, then optimize the remaining block contributions while tracking the unused vertex's total capacity, rather than maximizing each block independently. all-p-sharpness.mdConclusion: The candidate  $7p$  is supported by the explicit construction and exploratory optimization for four even values. Neither a counterexample nor an all- $p$  upper-bound proof has been obtained. Consequently, the proposed sharpness consequence for minimum degree three and maximum degrees  $15,20,25,\ldots$  remains unproved.I would keep this as an open extremal target rather than promote it as an established sharpness result.
